ti: MinRecordPrefixLen's rationale miscounts the encoding, so the six-character floor pins 28 timestamp bits, not 30

note: comment now states the real arithmetic: a p-char Crockford prefix pins 5p-2 timestamp bits (first char carries 3 payload bits), so p=6 pins 28 bits, a 2^20 ms (~17.5 min) mint window. TestPrefixPinsFivePMinusTwoTimestampBits pins the boundary from both sides (windowMs-1 shares the prefix, windowMs does not). Raising the floor to buy same-session stability is parked as an ADR-0013 amendment decision, not smuggled in here.

ti: MinRecordPrefixLen=6 pins only 28 timestamp bits (~17.5 min window): IDs minted in the same session but >17.5 min apart can share a 6-char prefix, so short prefixes are stable only within that window. Raise the floor to ~13 chars (pins 63 bits, prefix stable for the repo lifetime) at the cost of much longer visible IDs, or keep 6 and accept occasional re-disambiguation? This amends ADR-0013.
